name: Gilbert A. Pierce
bio: Gilbert A. Pierce of Chicago was appointed governor of Dakota Territory in July 1884, replacing Ordway, and was welcomed at Bismarck that August by a crowd of over 2,000. In March 1885 he vetoed the bill to move the capital from Bismarck to Pierre, and the paper praised the veto's legal reasoning. Through 1885 the Cow Boy followed efforts to remove him and backed him, while Medora waited on his ruling on Billings County's petition for organization. He set Arbor Day in 1885 and issued Thanksgiving proclamations in 1885 and 1886, his name appeared on the 1886 notices of the Billings County election, and in October 1886 he proclaimed a quarantine against cattle from Chicago and Illinois because of pleuro-pneumonia. In December 1886 the paper reported that he had declined to serve past January and would return to journalism.
